rules.rationale: Chalcogenide anions have moderate electronegativity; bonding-antibonding splitting yields larger gaps than halides.
High halide electronegativity raises valence band, reducing gap relative to chalcogenides at equal cation.
Metalloid-dominated covalent networks give strong sp hybridisation splitting and wide gaps.
Balanced compositions avoid metallic percolation pathways that collapse the gap.

skills.hypothesis: Source evidence links chalcogenide, metalloid, and balanced compositions to high refractive index; the same electron-rich covalent character should correlate with larger experimental band gaps, though halide-containing oxides may invert this.

rules.rationale: Counter-hypothesis: high-Z halides have diffuse valence orbitals and low experimental gaps, reversing source polarity.
Halogen-dominated compositions show strong anionic p character near the Fermi level, reducing gaps.
Lanthanide f states lie deep; source effect was near zero, so only a weak positive prior is defensible.
Partially filled d bands narrow gaps; source transfer weight here is low and uncertain.

skills.hypothesis: If source polarity does not transfer, halogen- and high-Z-rich chemistry should lower band gaps rather than raise them, so the surrogate should lean on the target-only anchor when these fields dominate.

fixed_initial.lesson: Anion chemistry dominates both properties, but chalcogenide and metalloid signals transfer more reliably than halogen and heavy-element signals; keep low-confidence source relations downweighted.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Retained the anion-family mechanism with added metalloid and balance rules, and introduced a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses halogen-dominant and heavy-element priors, selecting the chalcogenide/metalloid skill for deployment.

rules.rationale: Source halides lower refractive index; by the Moss relation low polarizability implies wide experimental gaps.
Compact valence orbitals in light constituents give large bonding-antibonding splitting and wide gaps.
Closed-shell main-group compounds lack partially filled d bands that pin the Fermi level.
Strongest source high-index effect; metalloid covalent networks (Si, Ge, Sb) are narrow-gap semiconductors.

skills.hypothesis: Merges inverted source polarity with light main-group ionic chemistry: halide, light-Z, main-group gain; metalloid loses. Fails if measured gaps track polarizability directly or halide entries are sparse.

rules.rationale: Counter-hypothesis: heavy-Z source effect is low-confidence, so its inverted penalty is downweighted toward neutral.
Deep O 2p valence bands and strong ionicity give oxides consistently wide experimental gaps.
Transition-metal oxides narrow via d-band charge-transfer states, offsetting the generic oxide ionicity bonus.
Selenides and tellurides are polarizable small-gap semiconductors; reverses the positive source chalcogenide prior.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the chalcogenide source prior and neutralizes the weakly supported heavy-Z relation, relying on oxide ionicity split by d-band chemistry. Fails if wide-gap entries are dominated by light sulfides or main-group heavy-Z halides.

true_feedback.lesson: Across two development generations the inverted-source and light main-group ionic proposals both scored far above the original chalcogenide/metalloid-positive prior, so Moss-type inversion plus main-group ionicity is the more durable prior; heavy-Z and lanthanide source relations carry too little support to justify strong weights.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Merged the two best-performing gen-1 skills into one deployment candidate that keeps the halide and metalloid inversions and adds the light-Z and main-group bonuses that drove the higher-AUC skill, dropping the low-support heavy-Z and lanthanide rules. Paired it with a counter-hypothesis skill that neutralizes the uncertain heavy-Z relation, reverses the chalcogenide source prior, and splits oxides by transition-metal charge-transfer character. Deployed the merged inverted skill.

rules.rationale: Closed-shell ionic halides have deep halogen p valence bands and no d states, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Oxygen 2p sits far below cation states, so oxides retain large ionic bonding-antibonding separation.
Polarizable S/Se/Te p bands raise the valence edge; high refractive index implies small gap by the Moss relation.
Light-element compounds have compact orbitals and strong sp splitting, favoring wide measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Refractive index and band gap are inversely related (Moss rule), so source-positive polarizable chemistries should be reversed: ionic halides and oxides maximize gaps. Fails if the target pool's halides are heavy-metal-containing.

rules.rationale: Strongest source effect: metalloid covalent networks keep large sp bonding-antibonding splitting.
Source chalcogenide effect was positive and well supported; chalcogen p covalency may also sustain semiconducting gaps.
Source pnictide effect was positive with moderate support; covalent pnictide bonding gives intermediate gaps.
Source halogen effect was clearly negative; carried across directly without polarity inversion.

skills.hypothesis: Direct sign-preserving transfer of the dielectric source effects: metalloid, chalcogenide and pnictide covalency up, halogen down. Fails if the Moss inverse relation dominates, since high-index materials are typically narrow-gap.

no_feedback.lesson: Source outcomes measure refractive index, which is physically anti-correlated with band gap, so sign-preserving transfer is unsafe; the deployed skill inverts polarizability-driven effects and favors ionic halide and oxide chemistry, with low semantic mass so the target-only anchor takes over as data accumulate.
no_feedback.revision_summary: Fixed schema by expressing every conditions block as a field-to-value object and capping rules at four. Replaced the prior direct-transfer deployment with a Moss-rule inversion skill (ionic halide/oxide/light-element positive, chalcogenide negative) and retained a sign-preserving source-grounded skill as the alternative; the inversion skill is selected.

rules.rationale: Source halides had the most negative refractive-index effect; by the Moss relation that low polarizability maps to wide experimental gaps.
Deep O 2p valence bands give large bonding-antibonding separation; oxides are also the cleanest wide-gap chemistry in this pool.
Chalcogenides carried the strongest positive source index effect, the polarizable soft-anion regime that narrows measured gaps.
Metalloid networks dominated the source high-index extremes; covalent Si/Ge/Sb-like networks are typically narrow-gap semiconductors.

skills.hypothesis: Sign-inverted source transfer plus chemistry-grounded oxide and soft-chalcogenide rules widens the effective gap estimate from polarizability alone. Fails where heavy iodides or defect-rich halides dominate the sampled compositions.

rules.rationale: Without partially filled d shells no mid-gap d states form, so measured optical gaps stay wide.
Low mean Z means short strong bonds and weak spin-orbit coupling, both pushing experimental gaps up.
Very heavy lattices are strongly polarizable with large spin-orbit splitting, which systematically narrows gaps.
Counter-hypothesis: concentrated compositions can sit near metallic connectivity, so the balanced-stoichiometry prior is only weakly supported and is downweighted.

skills.hypothesis: Domain proposal: wide experimental gaps arise from light, closed-shell chemistry with no d-band states, independent of anion identity. May fail for d0 wide-gap oxides such as titanates and for heavy closed-shell iodides.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Sign-inverted source transfer reproduced its development advantage across a second seed block, but the margin over the domain skill is small and both remain seed-sensitive; source effects rest on thin support counts and should stay near the anchor.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Kept the deployed Moss-inversion mechanism, retargeted it to anion-family polarizability with an added oxide wide-gap rule, and replaced the previous domain skill with one built on closed-shell cation hardness plus a downweighted stoichiometry counter-hypothesis; deployed the inverted anion-family transfer skill.
